title: Predict modification-dependent biochemical networks

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a model that predicts how combinations of chemical modifications to proteins change their activity, interactions and downstream biochemical responses in a cell. These post-translational modifications can regulate information transfer through interconnected enzyme and signaling networks. The intended capability would predict the direction, timing and magnitude of responses to previously untested modification combinations and enzyme perturbations within specified cellular contexts.

A modification's effect can depend on its location, accompanying modifications, timing, binding partners, enzyme availability and cellular environment; not every factor necessarily matters in every case. Site dependence alone can reverse an effect: the supplied review describes phosphorylation of RAF1 at S338 as stimulating catalytic activity, whereas phosphorylation at S259 attenuates activity. Detecting a modified site, or predicting that a site can be modified, therefore does not establish what that modification causes in a biochemical network.

Scope synthesis: The defining advance would be prospective, experimentally validated prediction of modification-dependent network behavior across multiple modification classes and cellular contexts. Better modification-site prediction, pathway enrichment or reconstruction of associated networks would contribute to this goal, but would not alone demonstrate it.

significance.text: Conditional significance: If achieved, this capability would turn many context-dependent signaling observations into quantitative hypotheses that researchers could test before performing an intervention. Predicting how local changes propagate through a network could help select informative perturbations, anticipate interacting effects and explain why the same modification produces different responses in different cells. The scientific basis for this possibility is the interconnected regulation of modifications by enzymes, through which changes in enzyme activity can affect processes throughout a cell.

Impact synthesis: Reliable predictions could improve intervention selection in research and, with additional validation, contribute to therapeutic development. Those downstream benefits remain conditional on measurement quality, model scope and the feasibility of manipulating the relevant processes. Predicting biochemical responses would not by itself deliver disease cures or arbitrary control of cell fate. No historical comparator was supplied, so a specific ranking against earlier scientific revolutions is not justified.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability is reliable causal prediction linking particular modification combinations to network responses in a specified cellular setting. Current measurements and computational associations leave several links uncertain: whether a detected site changes function, which molecular interactions mediate that effect, and how the effect propagates through enzyme-regulated networks. The review emphasizes incomplete functional annotations and notes that only some detectable modification sites appear to influence protein function, localization or interactions.

Measurement and interpretation must also resolve combinations and dynamics. Ambiguity about accompanying modifications can obscure which molecular state produced an observed response, while temporal occupancy and cellular context complicate comparisons between experiments. Enzyme substrate specificity measured in vitro does not establish that the enzyme and substrate encounter one another in a cell. These limitations make a list of possible modifications insufficient for predicting actual cellular responses.

The engineering challenge includes learning from uneven data without mistaking correlations for mechanisms. Phosphorylation-heavy coverage limits evidence for generalization across modification classes, and uncertain ground truths complicate evaluation. Models need independent benchmarks and targeted perturbation experiments capable of separating direct modification effects from downstream associations. Better performance on familiar pathways alone would leave the central generalization question unresolved.

current_state.text: The supplied research dates the review “Computational Approaches for Pathway-Centric Analysis of Protein Post-Translational Modifications,” by Julian Müller, Bernhard Kuster and Matthew The, to 18 October 2025. According to the supplied evidence review, it documents large-scale identification and quantification of multiple modification types using mass spectrometry, computational pathway-analysis tools, and selected analyses connecting multiple modification types with biochemical networks. These establish substantial measurement and analysis capabilities, without establishing general causal prediction.

The multi-modification examples require careful interpretation: coordinated regulation and inferred pathway connections should not all be described as experimentally demonstrated causal cross-talk. For example, the review describes DMPA as inferring correlations rather than causation, with undirected resulting networks. Its broader discussion identifies incomplete functional annotations, phosphorylation-heavy coverage, limitations of enrichment tools and a need for fair, independent benchmarks. The supplied evidence does not demonstrate a comprehensive model that predicts causal, context-dependent responses across modification classes.

Evidence scope: The supplied validated review reports inspecting an identity-verified, complete retained full-text XML copy, including article text, tables, captions and references; the source index reports no extraction issues or truncation. This record relies on that supplied assessment and does not claim a new inspection. The earlier account of a browser check and abstract-limited access is not substantiated by the retained evidence and should not constrain interpretation of the review. However, no bounded search record was supplied to establish subsequent developments through 1 November 2026. The dated review supports the scientific gap described here, but cannot establish that no later work changed the field's position.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: Evaluate a model prospectively across several independently chosen pathways and cellular contexts, using previously untested combinations of modifications and enzyme perturbations. Before experiments begin, specify pathway selection, response endpoints, timing windows and acceptable errors for predicted response direction, timing and magnitude. These are proposed evaluation requirements, not established consensus standards; the supplied materials do not justify particular numerical thresholds.
completion_criteria.label: Prospective predictions for untested perturbations meet prespecified response errors

completion_criteria.text: Proposed causal validation: Targeted experiments should reproduce the predicted responses and use controls that distinguish direct modification effects from downstream associations. Evaluation should avoid selecting only pathways already favorable to the model, and should include independent replication sufficient to assess reproducibility. These proposals respond to the review's calls for follow-up experimental validation and fair, independent benchmarking.
completion_criteria.label: Independent replication confirms predicted responses and direct modification effects

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundaries: A convincing result should state which modification classes, pathways, cellular contexts, perturbation ranges and time windows it covers, together with failures and uncertainty. Demonstrations should span multiple modification classes if they are to support the concept's intended breadth. A complete catalog of every possible modification is unnecessary, and finite experiments establish demonstrated breadth rather than literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Demonstrated modification network coverage is reported with failures and uncertainty

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison: BCH-05, “Routine, comprehensive single-cell proteoform reading,” concerns measuring distinct molecular forms of proteins, including their modification states. BCH-10 asks what those states do to biochemical networks. Better proteoform measurements could supply inputs and validation data, but measurement coverage and causal predictive capability remain separate achievements. BCH-02, “Predict biochemical function from molecular sequence and environment,” overlaps in predicting molecular function; BCH-10 specifically emphasizes interacting modification combinations, propagation through networks and cellular context.

Roster-based comparison: BCH-06, “A multiplexed biochemical flight recorder for living cells,” could provide temporal evidence useful for testing predicted response sequences. Recording biochemical events and predicting the causal consequences of modification perturbations are distinct capabilities. BCH-09, “Predict and control the biochemical organization of condensates,” could intersect where modifications alter molecular interactions or localization, but its focus is condensate organization, whereas BCH-10 concerns modification-dependent networks more broadly.

Roster-based comparison: BCH-01, “General design of enzymes for new chemical reactions,” could overlap through enzymes that install or remove modifications, while addressing a separate design problem. BCH-11, “Routine structural reading of complex glycans,” could contribute information where protein glycosylation matters; resolving glycan structure does not itself establish its functional network consequences. These possible connections do not make completion of either concept equivalent to completion of BCH-10.

Generalization beyond the pathways, modification classes and contexts actually tested would remain uncertain even after a successful bounded demonstration.

brief.title: Predicting how protein changes alter cell behavior
possible: Researchers could predict how a cell would respond before changing the chemical marks on its proteins. A model would forecast whether signals rise or fall, when they change and by how much—even for combinations of marks and changes to enzyme activity that have never been tested.
why: Chemical marks help regulate how proteins work and pass signals through a cell. Predicting their combined effects could help researchers choose more informative experiments and explain why the same mark produces different responses in different cells.
Reliable forecasts could also guide the choice of interventions for therapeutic development by anticipating how their effects interact.

sources.who: Julian Müller, Bernhard Kuster and Matthew The
sources.showed: Their review describes methods for measuring protein marks at scale and analyzing the connected chains of reactions they affect. It identifies gaps in knowledge about what those marks actually do.
sources.cited_for: Large-scale measurement and analysis already exist, but connecting protein marks to their functional effects remains difficult.
sources.not_established: The review does not demonstrate a model that predicts causal responses across different kinds of protein marks and cellular settings.

sources.who: Elin Nyman, Richard R Stein and colleagues
sources.showed: They modeled how proteins and cell behavior changed after drug treatment in a melanoma cell line. Experiments partly confirmed predictions of effective drug combinations.
sources.quote: Systematic model simulations identified novel combinations of drugs predicted to reduce the survival of melanoma cells, with partial experimental verification.
sources.cited_for: Models trained on responses over time can predict some previously untested drug combinations.
sources.not_established: Partial confirmation in a single cell line does not establish reliable prediction across protein-mark combinations and cellular settings.

sources.showed: Their model predicted changes in cell-signaling proteins over time under untested interventions. It ranked first in a breast cancer cell-line prediction challenge.
sources.quote: Furthermore, it was identified as the most consistent performer, defined as robustly ranked first when evaluated with a subset of data.
sources.cited_for: Predicting signaling responses to untested interventions has succeeded in a bounded challenge.
sources.not_established: The results do not establish causal prediction across multiple kinds of protein marks or reliable forecasts beyond the tested settings.

sources.who: Camille D A Terfve and colleagues
sources.showed: Their model traced effects through protein-signaling networks. In a breast cancer cell line, they confirmed a prediction linking mTOR and CDK2, enzymes that regulate protein activity.
sources.quote: We demonstrate the power of this approach by modelling the effect of the inhibition of multiple kinases in a breast cancer cell line and verify the unexpected prediction that mTOR inhibition affects the function of the cyclin-dependent kinase CDK2.
sources.cited_for: Targeted experiments can test unexpected connections predicted by a signaling-network model.
sources.not_established: Confirming a selected connection does not establish independent reproducibility or prediction across different kinds of protein marks.

shown: Researchers have predicted some responses to untested interventions in cancer cell lines. Nyman and colleagues partly confirmed predicted drug combinations, while Terfve and colleagues experimentally supported an unexpected signaling connection. These are bounded successes toward the broader capability.
missing: Reliable forecasts must connect untested combinations of protein marks to the direction, timing and size of cellular responses.
Experiments must distinguish effects caused directly by particular marks from changes that merely accompany them.
Measurements must distinguish combinations of marks and track how they change over time.
Independent tests must establish performance across different kinds of marks, reaction networks and cellular settings.

milestones.label: Untested interventions produce responses within agreed prediction errors
milestones.explanation: Prospective tests would have to meet preset errors for response direction, timing and size across independently chosen networks and cellular settings. This would establish prediction beyond familiar experiments.

milestones.label: Independent experiments reproduce responses and establish direct effects
milestones.explanation: Independent experiments would have to reproduce predicted responses, with controls separating direct effects of protein marks from downstream associations. This would establish reproducibility and causal support.

milestones.label: Demonstrated coverage includes failures and uncertainty
milestones.explanation: Results would have to report coverage across multiple kinds of marks, networks, cellular settings, intervention ranges and time windows, including failures and uncertainty. This would define where predictions can be trusted.

uncertain: The acceptable prediction errors, response measurements and amount of independent replication still need concrete definitions.
How often interacting protein marks have been shown to cause a response, rather than simply change together, remains unclear.
Success in tested settings would leave performance in other networks, kinds of marks and cellular environments uncertain.

page.title: Post-translational modification network prediction
page.definition: A model predicts how combinations of post-translational modifications—chemical changes to proteins after synthesis—and changes to their modifying enzymes alter biochemical network responses. It predicts response direction, magnitude and time course for previously untested interventions in specified cellular contexts.

goal.need: The A2058 melanoma study below illustrates the measurements collected for one cellular context. Its predicted drug combinations received partial experimental confirmation. Predicting untested responses connects molecular measurements to intervention selection, while exposing which effects remain experimentally unconfirmed.

figures.note: Dataset 1 had three biological replicates at every time point. Dataset 2 had one at six time points and three at 48 and 67 hours. Published on 15 July 2020.

completion.title: Prospective predictions of multi-PTM network responses replicate across cellular contexts.
completion.criterion: A fixed model prospectively predicts correct response directions and has lower root-mean-square trajectory error than both a no-change predictor and a version omitting PTM interactions, for a prespecified panel of untested modification combinations and enzyme perturbations involving at least two PTM classes in at least two cellular contexts. Targeted site perturbations confirm predicted causal dependencies. An independent laboratory repeats this result on new biological samples. The coverage minima and comparators are Atlas choices.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas fallback; no external completion criterion was located.
completion.basis: Searches of NIH PTM priorities, DARPA programmes, the 2025 PTM review and DREAM protocols found no acceptance test for prospective multi-PTM network prediction across cellular contexts. The fallback adds experimental replication as defined by the National Academies. Searches of 2026 crosstalk benchmarks also found no such test. The coverage minima and error comparators are Atlas choices.

milestones.title: A model predicts withheld phosphoprotein trajectories with lower error than random predictions.
milestones.criterion: Withhold an experimental intervention and predict its phosphoprotein time courses; root-mean-square error (RMSE) must be lower than the study's random-prediction baseline. Zhu and Guan's report of 11 June 2014 used 20 protein readouts, eight time points and three replicates in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells. Holding out the intermediate EGF stimulus gave RMSE 0.06 versus 0.91 for random predictions averaged over 100 runs. This tests stimulus interpolation within phosphorylation signalling.
milestones.set_by: Held-out predictive validation against a random baseline, as applied by Zhu and Guan in their experimental validation; the published test concerns phosphorylation.
milestones.threshold_quote: The predicted time course trajectory (red line) has a much lower RMSE across all the time points compared with random prediction (blue line).

milestones.title: A predicted signalling path produces both the expected phosphopeptide change and cellular response.
milestones.criterion: A predicted signalling path produces the expected substrate-phosphorylation and cellular responses after targeted inhibition. On 10 September 2015, Terfve et al. reported that Akt or mTORC1/2 inhibition reduced a CCNL1 phosphopeptide 2–5-fold; after 24 hours, MCF7 cells' G1 fractions rose about 1.7- and 2-fold, respectively. P70S6K inhibition did not produce the phosphopeptide decrease. Flow cytometry used 5,000 cells per injection and three technical injections per sample. These results support the proposed mTOR–Akt–CDK2 path.
milestones.set_by: Experimental testing of model predictions, used by the PHONEMeS developers in Figure 5 and by the perturbation-biology developers for drug-combination validation; the PHONEMeS test concerns phosphorylation.
milestones.threshold_quote: verify the unexpected prediction that mTOR inhibition affects the function of the cyclin-dependent kinase CDK2.

milestones.title: A model earns DREAM top-performer status for blind phosphoprotein time-course prediction.
milestones.criterion: Receive organizer-designated top-performer status in DREAM SC2A: predict withheld mTOR-inhibition phosphoprotein trajectories in four breast cancer cell lines under eight stimuli, from 0 to 4 hours. Predictions are ranked by log-scale RMSE. Robust superiority requires outranking another team in at least 75 of 100 subsamples, retaining 50% of data. The organizers' 22 February 2016 report named Team42 and Team10 as top performers; the nominal first-ranked submission was incomplete.
milestones.set_by: HPN-DREAM Breast Cancer Network Inference Challenge organizers, time-course prediction scoring and ranking-robustness methods; this challenge concerns phosphorylation.
milestones.threshold_quote: Team A was considered to be robustly ranked above team B if the former outranked the latter in at least 75% of iterations.

milestones.title: Untested combinations of two PTM classes produce the predicted network responses in one cellular context.
milestones.criterion: In one specified cellular context, a fixed model prospectively predicts correct response directions for a prespecified panel of untested combinations involving at least two PTM classes and perturbations of their modifying enzymes. Its root-mean-square trajectory error is lower than both a no-change predictor and a version omitting PTM interactions. Targeted site perturbations support the predicted causal dependencies. ProteinNexus's 11 May 2026 report used computational knockouts on two sequences involving phosphorylation/SUMOylation or glycosylation/phosphorylation; these do not establish this cellular result.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas fallback; searches of NIH priorities, PTM pathway reviews and subsequent crosstalk benchmarks found no external prospective multi-PTM network threshold. The class minimum and comparators are Atlas choices.

not_found: No external completion test specifying PTM-class coverage, cellular-context coverage and predictive-error limits was found.
No prospective experimental result satisfying the multi-PTM milestone or independently replicated completion test was located.
The main text did not identify a biological replicate count for the PHONEMeS cell-cycle validation; its stated triplicates were instrument injections.

results.finding: A2058 models predicted withheld molecular and phenotype data across 10 models, with mean error 0.181.
results.detail: The test included protein and phosphoprotein trajectories for held-out drug combinations, but the reported error combines molecular and phenotypic nodes. No random-prediction baseline is reported.
results.quote: The resulting generalization error for optimal λ* on left-out data had a mean of 0.181 across the 10 models and of 0.118 for phenotypic data alone, and the corresponding Pearson correlation coefficient between model prediction and the experimentally measured data was 0.54 (molecular and phenotypic) and 0.79 for the phenotypic data alone.

results.finding: Predicted NT157–gefitinib treatment reduced A2058 cell growth in three replicates.
results.detail: The predicted cellular response was observed, but the study did not establish the predicted phosphorylation change: the authors state that NT157's effect on IRS1-pS636/639 was unknown.
results.quote: The drug pair with the strongest predicted effect, NT157 and gefitinib, reduced cell growth substantially relative to no-drug control, and the combination is more effective than the effect of either drug alone

results.finding: For 20 protein readouts, the withheld EGF trajectory prediction had RMSE 0.06 versus 0.91 for random predictions.
results.detail: MDA-MB-468 cells; eight time points and three replicates. The model trained on 0 and 10 ng EGF and predicted the withheld 5 ng condition.
results.quote: The average RMSE for the eight time points is 0.06, while random prediction baseline (for 100 runs) is 0.91, indicating 15-fold reductions in error.

results.finding: The model achieved top performance in a 2013 DREAM 8 breast cancer time-course challenge; sample size is not stated.
results.detail: The paper reports challenge performance but does not establish the specified SC2A conditions, organizer-designated Team42 or Team10 status, or the 75-of-100 subsample criterion.
results.quote: This algorithm achieved the top performance in the 2013 8th Dialogue for Reverse Engineering Assessments and Methods (DREAM 8) subchallenge: time course prediction in breast cancer cell lines.

results.finding: In MCF7 cells, Akt and mTORC1/2 inhibition increased G1 fractions about 1.7- and 2-fold; flow cytometry analyzed 5,000 cells per injection.
results.detail: The CCNL1 phosphopeptide decreased 2–5-fold after Akt or mTORC1/2 inhibition, but not P70S6K inhibition. Cell-cycle analysis followed 24 hours of treatment, with three technical injections per sample.
results.quote:
As we can see in
Fig. 5d
, on pharmacological inhibition of either Akt or mTORC1/2, the proportion of cells present in G1 phase increased approximately 1.7- and 2-fold, respectively, relative to DMSO control, and the proportion of cells present in S and G2/M phase was concomitantly reduced.

results.detail: Team42 ranked second and Team10 ranked third. The first-ranked submission, Team44, was incomplete and ineligible for top-performer status.
